baseBranchPatterns: NOTE: this list is replaced at run time. runai-actions .github/workflows/renovate.yml runs renovate/scan_candidates, which finds the newest release branches in this repository and starts one Renovate run per branch, each scoped to its own. This line is not a branch pattern and matches nothing, so a run that skips that step scans nothing rather than everything.
includePaths: NOTE: the rest of this list is added at run time. runai-actions .github/workflows/renovate.yml runs renovate/scan_candidates, which adds every Go module it finds safe to bump. Keep only entries it cannot work out from the module layout, such as a folder holding no Go module. This line is not a path and is dropped before the list reaches Renovate.

packageRules.description: frontend and frontend-v2 are two separate npm apps that happen to share a folder. Keep them in separate PRs rather than letting the folder-based group key merge them.

A prettier bump changes how prettier formats existing, untouched source: 3.4.2 to 3.9.6 collapses short union types onto one line, reformatting 33 files under control-plane/frontend. `npm run format` runs prettier --check, so the upgrade fails its own lint job and can never merge. The script reformats with the version the branch is adopting, so the PR carries the churn its own upgrade causes. It is a no-op for packages that do not depend on prettier.

The frontend takes Dockerfile updates only. npm bumps break it faster than the guild can absorb them: typescript 5.3->5.9 and @vue/test-utils 2.4.6->2.4.11 together produced TS2589/TS2307/TS2339 plus failing vitest suites, and the four resulting PRs sat red for days with no owner. Closing them only made Renovate reopen them, so switch the manager off rather than keep generating work nobody can merge. This is deliberately absolute: it also stops npm vulnerability remediation for the frontend, which is a tradeoff owned outside Renovate. The dockerfile rule above is unaffected, so base-image updates keep flowing.
